AD.name: Andorra
facts: Andorra is the sixth-smallest nation in Europe, nestled in the Pyrenees mountains between France and Spain.
Andorra has no airport, railway, or motorway — visitors arrive by road.
Tourism and duty-free shopping account for about 80% of Andorra's GDP.
Andorra la Vella is the highest capital city in Europe at 1,023 meters.
Andorra has one of the highest life expectancies in the world at over 83 years.

AE.name: UAE
facts: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world at 828 meters.
The UAE has the world's first 3D-printed office building.
Dubai's Palm Jumeirah is the world's largest artificial island.
The UAE went from a desert economy to one of the wealthiest nations in just 50 years.
The UAE has seven emirates, each with its own ruler.

AF.name: Afghanistan
facts: Afghanistan is home to the famous Bamiyan Valley, once housing two giant Buddha statues carved in the 6th century.
The national sport of Afghanistan is Buzkashi, a horseback game played with a goat carcass.
Afghanistan has over 200 days of sunshine per year.
The country sits at the crossroads of Central and South Asia, making it historically vital for trade routes.
Afghanistan's Hindu Kush mountain range has peaks over 7,000 meters.

AG.name: Antigua and Barbuda
facts: Antigua and Barbuda has 365 beaches — one for every day of the year.
Cricket is the national sport, and the country has produced world-class players like Viv Richards.
Barbuda's Frigate Bird Sanctuary is the largest in the Western Hemisphere.
The country gained independence from Britain in 1981.
Antigua was once the headquarters of the British Royal Navy in the Caribbean.

AL.name: Albania
facts: Albania has over 750,000 bunkers built during the communist era — more bunkers per capita than any country.
Mother Teresa, the Nobel Peace Prize winner, was of Albanian origin.
Albania was one of the last European countries to allow private car ownership, banning them until 1991.
The country has a tradition called 'besa' — a code of honor meaning 'to keep the promise.'
Albania's coast has both the Adriatic and Ionian seas.

AM.name: Armenia
facts: Armenia was the first country to adopt Christianity as a state religion in 301 AD.
The Armenian alphabet was created in 405 AD and has 39 letters.
Armenia is home to the world's oldest leather shoe, dating back 5,500 years.
Chess is a mandatory school subject in Armenia.
Mount Ararat, where Noah's Ark is said to have landed, is visible from Armenia's capital.

AO.name: Angola
facts: Angola is the second-largest oil producer in sub-Saharan Africa.
The Kalandula Falls in Angola are among the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume.
Angola's capital Luanda was once ranked the most expensive city in the world for expatriates.
The country has a giant sable antelope, found nowhere else on Earth.
Angola shares its name with the Ngola dynasty that once ruled the region.

AR.name: Argentina
facts: Argentina is named after the Latin word for silver — 'argentum.'
The tango dance originated in the working-class neighborhoods of Buenos Aires.
Argentina has the widest avenue in the world — Avenida 9 de Julio has 14 lanes.
Patagonia in southern Argentina contains one of the world's largest dinosaur fossil sites.
Argentina was the first country to use fingerprinting as a method of identification.

AT.name: Austria
facts: Austria's flag is one of the oldest national flags in the world, dating back to 1230.
Vienna has been ranked the world's most livable city multiple times.
The croissant was invented in Vienna to celebrate victory over the Ottoman Empire.
Mozart, Beethoven, Schubert, and Strauss all lived and worked in Vienna.
Austria is 62% covered by the Alps.

AU.name: Australia
facts: Australia is both a country and a continent — the only nation to occupy an entire continent.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth, visible from space.
Australia has more than 10,000 beaches — you could visit a new one every day for 27 years.
The Australian Alps receive more snowfall than the Swiss Alps.
Kangaroos and emus can't walk backward, which is why they're on Australia's coat of arms — symbolizing progress.

AZ.name: Azerbaijan
facts: Azerbaijan is known as the 'Land of Fire' due to natural gas flames that seep from the ground.
Baku's Flame Towers are shaped like flames and are covered in LED screens.
Azerbaijan was the first Muslim-majority country to grant women the right to vote in 1918.
The country has mud volcanoes — more than half of the world's total.
The Maiden Tower in Baku dates back to the 12th century.

BA.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
facts: Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in 1914 triggered World War I.
Bosnia has the last remaining primeval forest in Europe — Perućica.
The country has more than 25 natural mineral springs.
The Stari Most bridge in Mostar, built in 1566, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

BB.name: Barbados
facts: Barbados became a republic in 2021, removing the British monarch as head of state.
Rihanna was born in Barbados and is a national hero of the country.
Barbados has the third-oldest parliament in the Commonwealth, established in 1639.
The island is the birthplace of rum — Mount Gay Distillery has been producing since 1703.
Barbados is the most easterly Caribbean island.

BD.name: Bangladesh
facts: Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries in the world.
The Sundarbans mangrove forest, shared with India, is the largest in the world and home to Bengal tigers.
The national anthem of Bangladesh was written by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.
Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China.
Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh has the longest unbroken sea beach in the world at 120 km.

BE.name: Belgium
facts: Belgium produces over 220,000 tonnes of chocolate per year.
The saxophone was invented by Belgian Adolphe Sax in the 1840s.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French, and German.
Brussels is the de facto capital of the European Union.
Belgium has more comic book artists per square mile than any other country.

BF.name: Burkina Faso
facts: Burkina Faso means 'Land of Honest People' in the local Mossi and Dyula languages.
FESPACO, Africa's largest film festival, is held in Ouagadougou every two years.
Burkina Faso was formerly called Upper Volta until 1984.
The country has one of the youngest populations in the world with a median age around 17.
Burkina Faso's Ruins of Loropéni are a UNESCO World Heritage Site dating back to the 11th century.

BG.name: Bulgaria
facts: Bulgaria is the oldest country in Europe that hasn't changed its name since it was first established in 681 AD.
Bulgarians shake their head for 'yes' and nod for 'no' — the opposite of most countries.
The Cyrillic alphabet was developed in Bulgaria in the 9th century.
Bulgarian yogurt contains a unique bacteria — Lactobacillus bulgaricus — found nowhere else.
Bulgaria has been producing rose oil for perfumes for over 300 years.

BH.name: Bahrain
facts: Bahrain is an archipelago of 33 islands in the Persian Gulf.
The Tree of Life in Bahrain has survived for over 400 years in the desert with no apparent water source.
Bahrain was the first Gulf state to discover oil in 1932.
The Bahrain Grand Prix was the first Formula 1 race held in the Middle East.
Bahrain's name means 'Two Seas' in Arabic, referring to freshwater springs beneath the sea.

BI.name: Burundi
facts: Burundi is one of the smallest countries in Africa but one of the most densely populated.
Drumming is a sacred tradition in Burundi — the Royal Drummers of Burundi are world-famous.
Lake Tanganyika, bordering Burundi, is the second-deepest lake in the world.
Burundi moved its capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2019.
The country's economy is heavily dependent on coffee, which accounts for most export earnings.

BJ.name: Benin
facts: Benin is considered the birthplace of Vodun (Voodoo), still widely practiced there.
The Kingdom of Dahomey, based in modern Benin, had an all-female military unit — the Dahomey Amazons.
Benin's Ganvié is the largest lake village in Africa, built entirely on stilts.
The country was formerly known as Dahomey until 1975.
Benin has one of the highest rates of twin births in the world.

BN.name: Brunei
facts: Brunei's Sultan is one of the wealthiest people in the world.
The country has no income tax for its citizens.
Brunei's Istana Nurul Iman is the largest residential palace in the world with 1,788 rooms.
Brunei is one of the smallest countries in Asia, located on the island of Borneo.
Oil and gas account for over 90% of Brunei's export earnings.

BO.name: Bolivia
facts: Bolivia has 37 official languages, one of the most in any country.
The Salar de Uyuni is the world's largest salt flat, covering 10,582 square kilometers.
La Paz, Bolivia's administrative capital, is the highest capital city in the world at 3,640 meters.
Bolivia is named after Simón Bolívar, the South American independence leader.
Bolivia is one of only two landlocked countries in South America.

BR.name: Brazil
facts: Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas.
The Amazon Rainforest produces about 20% of the world's oxygen.
Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup a record 5 times.
São Paulo has the largest Japanese population outside Japan.
Brazil's coastline stretches over 7,400 km — longer than the distance from New York to London.

BS.name: Bahamas
facts: The Bahamas consists of over 700 islands and cays, but only about 30 are inhabited.
The swimming pigs of Exuma have become a major tourist attraction.
The Bahamas has the third-largest barrier reef in the world.
Columbus made his first landfall in the New World on San Salvador island in the Bahamas.
Dean's Blue Hole in the Bahamas is the deepest known saltwater blue hole at over 200 meters.

BT.name: Bhutan
facts: Bhutan measures national success by Gross National Happiness instead of GDP.
Bhutan is the only carbon-negative country in the world, absorbing more CO2 than it produces.
Television and the internet were not introduced in Bhutan until 1999.
Archery is the national sport of Bhutan.
Bhutan's Tiger's Nest Monastery clings to a cliffside 3,000 meters above sea level.

BW.name: Botswana
facts: Botswana's Okavango Delta is the world's largest inland delta and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Botswana has one of the highest elephant populations in the world — over 130,000.
The country is one of Africa's most stable democracies since independence in 1966.
Botswana's diamond industry makes it one of the wealthiest countries in Africa per capita.
The Kalahari Desert covers about 70% of Botswana's land area.

BY.name: Belarus
facts: Belarus is one of the most forested countries in Europe — about 40% is covered by trees.
The European bison, once nearly extinct, roams free in Belarus's Białowieża Forest.
Belarus means 'White Russia' in its language.
Minsk was almost entirely rebuilt after being destroyed in World War II.
Belarus has one of the highest literacy rates in the world at over 99%.

BZ.name: Belize
facts: Belize is the only Central American country where English is the official language.
The Great Blue Hole off Belize's coast is a giant marine sinkhole over 300 meters across and 125 meters deep.
Belize has the largest cave system in Central America.
The Belize Barrier Reef is the second largest in the world after Australia's.
Ancient Maya ruins like Caracol and Xunantunich are found throughout Belize.

CA.name: Canada
facts: Canada has the longest coastline in the world at over 202,080 km.
Canada has more lakes than all other countries combined.
The Trans-Canada Highway is one of the longest national highways in the world at 7,821 km.
Canada produces 71% of the world's maple syrup.
The Canadian territory of Nunavut is larger than Western Europe but has a population of only about 40,000.

CD.name: DR Congo
facts: The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, reaching depths of over 220 meters.
DR Congo contains over half of Africa's tropical rainforest.
The country has massive deposits of coltan, essential for making smartphones and laptops.
Kinshasa and Brazzaville are the two closest capital cities in the world, separated only by the Congo River.
DR Congo is the largest country in sub-Saharan Africa.

CF.name: Central African Republic
facts: The Central African Republic is home to lowland gorillas and forest elephants.
Dzanga-Sangha is one of the best places in Africa to see western lowland gorillas in the wild.
The CAR has some of the richest diamond deposits in Africa.
The Ubangi River forms the southern border and is a major tributary of the Congo.
The country's flag uniquely combines Pan-African and French Tricolore colors.

CG.name: Republic of the Congo
facts: Brazzaville and Kinshasa (DR Congo) face each other across the Congo River — the closest capital cities in the world.
The Republic of the Congo has some of the largest intact rainforests in Africa.
The country is a major oil producer in Central Africa.
The Batéké Plateau in the south has unique grasslands and deep canyons.
Congo-Brazzaville was the first African country to adopt a Marxist government in 1970.

CH.name: Switzerland
facts: Switzerland has four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh.
Switzerland hasn't been in a war since 1815, maintaining armed neutrality.
The country has enough nuclear bunker space to shelter its entire population.
The Swiss consume more chocolate per capita than any other nation — about 10 kg per person per year.
Switzerland's flag is one of only two square sovereign-state flags (the other is Vatican City).

CI.name: Côte d'Ivoire
facts: Côte d'Ivoire is the world's largest producer of cocoa beans.
The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in Yamoussoukro is the largest church in the world.
Abidjan is the economic capital and largest city, despite Yamoussoukro being the official capital.
The country's name literally means 'Ivory Coast' and it requests not to be translated.
Côte d'Ivoire has won two Africa Cup of Nations football titles.

CL.name: Chile
facts: Chile is the longest north-south country in the world, stretching 4,300 km.
The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest place on Earth — some areas haven't seen rain in over 400 years.
Chile has the world's largest swimming pool at the San Alfonso del Mar resort — over 1 km long.
Easter Island (Rapa Nui), with its famous Moai statues, belongs to Chile.
Chile was the first South American country to legalize same-sex marriage.

CM.name: Cameroon
facts: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature' because it contains all of Africa's major climates and vegetation.
Mount Cameroon is the highest peak in West Africa and is an active volcano.
The name 'Cameroon' comes from Portuguese explorers who named it 'Rio dos Camarões' (River of Shrimp).
Cameroon has over 250 different ethnic groups.
Cameroon's football team, the Indomitable Lions, was the first African team to reach a World Cup quarter-final.

CN.name: China
facts: The Great Wall of China stretches over 21,000 km and took more than 2,000 years to build.
China invented paper, printing, gunpowder, and the compass — known as the Four Great Inventions.
All pandas in the world belong to China — those in foreign zoos are on loan.
China has the world's fastest commercial train — the Shanghai Maglev reaches 431 km/h.
The Terracotta Army in Xi'an has over 8,000 unique soldier statues, each with a different face.

CO.name: Colombia
facts: Colombia is the only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific and Caribbean.
Colombia produces more emeralds than any other country — about 70-90% of the world's supply.
The country is named after Christopher Columbus, though he never set foot there.
Colombia is the second most biodiverse country in the world after Brazil.
Bogotá's Ciclovía closes 120 km of roads to cars every Sunday for cyclists and pedestrians.

CR.name: Costa Rica
facts: Costa Rica has no army — it was abolished in 1948 and the budget redirected to education and healthcare.
The country contains 5% of the world's biodiversity despite being only 0.03% of the planet's surface.
Costa Rica consistently ranks among the happiest countries in the world.
'Pura Vida' (Pure Life) is the national motto and greeting.
Costa Rica generates over 98% of its electricity from renewable sources.

CU.name: Cuba
facts: Cuba has one of the highest literacy rates in the world at 99.8%.
Classic American cars from the 1950s still fill Cuban streets because of a decades-long trade embargo.
Cuba has more doctors per capita than most developed nations.
The island was the first place Christopher Columbus landed in the Americas in 1492.
Cuban cigars are considered the finest in the world due to the island's unique soil.

CV.name: Cabo Verde
facts: Cabo Verde is a volcanic archipelago of 10 islands off the west coast of Africa.
The islands were uninhabited until Portuguese settlers arrived in the 15th century.
Cesária Évora, the 'Barefoot Diva,' brought Cabo Verdean music to international fame.
Cabo Verde has one of the most stable democracies in Africa.
The country's name means 'Green Cape' in Portuguese, though the islands are mostly arid.

CY.name: Cyprus
facts: Nicosia is the last divided capital in the world, split between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.
Cyprus is the third-largest island in the Mediterranean Sea.
According to Greek mythology, Aphrodite, the goddess of love, was born on the shores of Cyprus.
Cyprus has been inhabited for over 10,000 years.
Halloumi cheese originated in Cyprus and is a major export product.

CZ.name: Czechia
facts: Czechia has the highest beer consumption per capita in the world.
Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle in the world according to Guinness World Records.
The word 'robot' was coined by Czech writer Karel Čapek in 1920.
The soft contact lens was invented by Czech chemist Otto Wichterle.
Czechia is one of the least religious countries in the world.

DE.name: Germany
facts: Germany has over 1,500 different beers and hosts the world-famous Oktoberfest.
The printing press was invented by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz, Germany around 1440.
Germany's Autobahn has sections with no speed limit.
Berlin has more bridges than Venice — approximately 960.
Germany is the birthplace of Kindergarten — the word means 'children's garden.'

DJ.name: Djibouti
facts: Djibouti sits at the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world.
Lake Assal in Djibouti is the lowest point in Africa at 155 meters below sea level.
Several countries including the US, China, France, and Japan maintain military bases in Djibouti.
Djibouti is one of the hottest countries on Earth with temperatures often exceeding 40°C.
The country is roughly the size of New Jersey.

DK.name: Denmark
facts: Denmark's flag (Dannebrog) is the oldest state flag in the world still in use, dating to 1219.
LEGO was invented in Denmark — the name comes from 'leg godt' meaning 'play well.'
No point in Denmark is more than 52 km from the sea.
Denmark is consistently ranked as one of the happiest countries in the world.
The concept of 'hygge' — Danish coziness and comfortable living — has become famous worldwide.

DM.name: Dominica
facts: Dominica is known as the 'Nature Isle of the Caribbean' for its lush rainforests.
Dominica's flag features a Sisserou parrot, the national bird found only on the island.
Boiling Lake in Dominica is the second-largest thermally active lake in the world.
Dominica has 365 rivers — one for each day of the year.
The island was the last Caribbean island to be colonized by Europeans due to fierce resistance by the Kalinago people.

DO.name: Dominican Republic
facts: Santo Domingo is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas, founded in 1496.
The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.
The country has produced more Major League Baseball players per capita than any other nation.
Pico Duarte is the highest peak in the Caribbean at 3,098 meters.
Larimar, a rare blue gemstone, is found only in the Dominican Republic.

DZ.name: Algeria
facts: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.
About 80% of Algeria's land area is the Sahara Desert.
The ancient Roman city of Timgad in Algeria is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Algeria gained independence from France in 1962 after a brutal 8-year war.
The country has the 16th-largest oil reserves in the world.

EC.name: Ecuador
facts: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through the country.
The Galápagos Islands, belonging to Ecuador, inspired Darwin's theory of evolution.
Ecuador was the first country to constitutionally recognize the rights of nature.
Panama hats actually originate from Ecuador, not Panama.
Ecuador uses the US dollar as its official currency.

EE.name: Estonia
facts: Estonia is one of the most digitally advanced countries — citizens can vote, pay taxes, and sign documents online.
Skype was originally created by Estonian developers.
Estonia has more startups per capita than most European countries.
Tallinn's Old Town is one of the best-preserved medieval cities in Europe.
Estonia's e-Residency program allows anyone in the world to start an EU-based business online.

EG.name: Egypt
facts: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest man-made structure for nearly 4,000 years.
Ancient Egyptians invented one of the first writing systems — hieroglyphics.
Egypt's Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and handles 12% of global trade.
Cairo is the largest city in Africa and the Arab world.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.

ER.name: Eritrea
facts: Asmara's Art Deco architecture earned it a UNESCO World Heritage Site designation.
Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993 after a 30-year war.
The Dahlak Archipelago off Eritrea's coast has pristine coral reefs and over 200 islands.
Eritrea has nine recognized ethnic groups, each with its own language.
The country's name comes from the Greek word 'Erythra,' meaning 'red,' referring to the Red Sea.

ES.name: Spain
facts: Spain's La Tomatina festival involves throwing over 150,000 tomatoes in a town-wide food fight.
Spain has the second-highest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the world.
The Spanish Steps are actually in Rome — but the Spanish language is the 4th most spoken in the world.
Spain's tradition of siesta (afternoon nap) is still practiced in many regions.
The Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882.

ET.name: Ethiopia
facts: Ethiopia is the only African country that was never colonized.
Ethiopia follows a unique calendar that is 7-8 years behind the Gregorian calendar and has 13 months.
Coffee was discovered in Ethiopia — legend says a goat herder noticed his goats dancing after eating coffee berries.
Lucy, one of the oldest known human ancestors (3.2 million years), was found in Ethiopia.
Ethiopia's Danakil Depression is one of the hottest inhabited places on Earth.

FI.name: Finland
facts: Finland has over 3 million saunas for a population of 5.6 million — roughly one per household.
Finland is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' but actually has 188,000 lakes.
Finland's education system is ranked among the best in the world, with no standardized tests.
Finland was the first country in Europe to give women the right to vote in 1906.
Santa Claus is officially recognized as living in Rovaniemi, Finland.

FJ.name: Fiji
facts: Fiji consists of over 330 islands, of which about 110 are permanently inhabited.
Fiji was one of the first places in the world to see each new day due to its proximity to the International Date Line.
The traditional Fijian drink kava is made from the root of a pepper plant and has mild sedative effects.
Fiji's rugby sevens team won the country's first Olympic gold medal in 2016.
The Great Astrolabe Reef surrounding Fiji is one of the largest barrier reefs in the world.

FM.name: Micronesia
facts: Micronesia consists of over 600 islands spread across the western Pacific Ocean.
Nan Madol, an ancient city built on artificial islands, is sometimes called the 'Venice of the Pacific.'
Micronesia has some of the best wreck diving in the world, from WWII-era ships in Chuuk Lagoon.
The country uses the US dollar as its official currency.
Traditional navigation using stars, wave patterns, and bird flight is still practiced.

FR.name: France
facts: France is the most visited country in the world with over 89 million tourists annually.
The Eiffel Tower was meant to be temporary — it was built for the 1889 World's Fair.
France has the most time zones of any country (12) due to its overseas territories.
French law requires that at least 40% of music on French radio must be of French origin.
The Louvre in Paris is the most visited art museum in the world.

GA.name: Gabon
facts: About 88% of Gabon is covered by tropical rainforest.
Gabon has 13 national parks covering 11% of the country's land area.
Lopé National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with both rainforest and savanna.
Gabon is one of the most urbanized countries in Africa, with over 85% living in cities.
Albert Schweitzer built his famous hospital in Lambaréné, Gabon in 1913.

GB.name: United Kingdom
facts: The British Empire was the largest empire in history, covering about 25% of the world's land.
London's Big Ben is actually the name of the bell, not the clock tower.
The UK invented the World Wide Web — Tim Berners-Lee created it in 1989.
The Queen's Guard at Buckingham Palace are active soldiers who can arrest you.
English is spoken as a first or second language by over 1.5 billion people worldwide.

GD.name: Grenada
facts: Grenada is known as the 'Spice Isle' because it produces a third of the world's nutmeg.
The country's flag features a nutmeg, reflecting its importance to the economy.
Grenada has the world's first underwater sculpture park off its coast.
Grand Anse Beach in Grenada is consistently ranked among the best beaches in the Caribbean.
Grenada gained independence from Britain in 1974.

GE.name: Georgia
facts: Georgia is one of the oldest wine-producing regions in the world — winemaking dates back 8,000 years.
The Georgian alphabet is one of only 14 unique writing systems in the world.
Georgia's Caucasus Mountains contain Europe's highest settlement, Ushguli, at 2,200 meters.
Stalin was born in Gori, Georgia.
Georgia's cuisine, especially khachapuri (cheese bread) and khinkali (dumplings), is gaining global fame.

GH.name: Ghana
facts: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule in 1957.
Ghana is the second-largest producer of cocoa in the world.
Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world by surface area.
Ghana is known for its colorful fantasy coffins, shaped like animals, cars, or symbols of the deceased's life.
The name 'Ghana' means 'Warrior King' in the Soninke language.

GM.name: Gambia
facts: Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa.
The country is essentially a narrow strip of land on either side of the Gambia River.
Gambia is almost entirely surrounded by Senegal.
Kunta Kinteh Island (formerly James Island) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site linked to the slave trade.
The Gambia River is one of the finest waterways in West Africa and the country's lifeline.

GN.name: Guinea
facts: Guinea has the world's largest reserves of bauxite, the ore used to make aluminum.
The Niger, Senegal, and Gambia rivers all originate in Guinea's Fouta Djallon highlands.
Guinea was the first French-speaking African country to gain independence in 1958.
Mount Nimba, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, straddles Guinea's border with Côte d'Ivoire and Liberia.
Guinea's diverse landscape includes coastal mangroves, savanna, and highland forests.

GQ.name: Equatorial Guinea
facts: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language.
The country has one of the highest GDPs per capita in Africa due to oil wealth.
Bioko Island, where the capital Malabo is located, is a volcanic island in the Gulf of Guinea.
The country is planning to move its capital to Ciudad de la Paz on the mainland.
Equatorial Guinea has three official languages: Spanish, French, and Portuguese.

GR.name: Greece
facts: Greece is considered the birthplace of democracy, philosophy, and the Olympic Games.
Greece has more archaeological museums than any other country in the world.
The Greek language has been spoken for over 3,400 years, making it one of the oldest living languages.
Greece has over 6,000 islands, but only about 227 are inhabited.
The marathon race is named after a Greek soldier who ran from Marathon to Athens — about 42 km.

GT.name: Guatemala
facts: Guatemala's currency is named after the Quetzal bird, which was sacred to the ancient Maya.
Tikal, one of the largest ancient Maya cities, is in Guatemala's Petén jungle.
Guatemala is the most populous country in Central America.
The ancient Maya invented chocolate — cacao was used as currency in Guatemala.
Lake Atitlán, surrounded by volcanoes, is often called the most beautiful lake in the world.

GW.name: Guinea-Bissau
facts: Guinea-Bissau's Bijagós Archipelago is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve with unique wildlife.
Cashew nuts are the country's main export product.
Guinea-Bissau gained independence from Portugal in 1973 after an 11-year guerrilla war.
The country is one of the smallest in West Africa.
The Bijagós Islands are home to saltwater hippos — one of the few places they exist.

GY.name: Guyana
facts: Guyana is the only English-speaking country in South America.
Kaieteur Falls in Guyana is one of the most powerful waterfalls in the world by volume and height.
Over 80% of Guyana is covered by tropical rainforest.
Guyana recently discovered massive offshore oil reserves, transforming its economy.
The country's name comes from an indigenous word meaning 'Land of Many Waters.'

HN.name: Honduras
facts: Honduras is home to the ancient Maya ruins of Copán, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Bay Islands off Honduras have some of the world's best reef diving.
Honduras means 'depths' in Spanish, named by Columbus for the deep waters off its coast.
La Mosquitia in eastern Honduras is one of the largest wilderness areas in Central America.
Honduras has the second-largest barrier reef in the world as part of the Mesoamerican Reef.

HR.name: Croatia
facts: The necktie (cravat) originated in Croatia — Croatian soldiers wore them in the 17th century.
Dubrovnik's Old Town was a filming location for King's Landing in Game of Thrones.
Croatia has over 1,200 islands along its Adriatic coast.
Plitvice Lakes National Park has 16 terraced lakes connected by waterfalls.
Croatia's Dalmatian coast is named after the region — and so is the Dalmatian dog breed.

HT.name: Haiti
facts: Haiti was the first independent Black republic, gaining freedom from France in 1804.
Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.
The Citadelle Laferrière is the largest fortress in the Americas.
Haiti's revolution was the only successful large-scale slave revolt in history.
Haitian art, especially its vibrant paintings and metalwork, is celebrated worldwide.

HU.name: Hungary
facts: The Rubik's Cube was invented by Hungarian professor Ernő Rubik in 1974.
Budapest has the largest thermal water cave system in the world.
Hungary has won more Olympic gold medals per capita than most countries.
The Hungarian language is unrelated to any neighboring country's language.
Budapest's Parliament Building is the third largest in the world.

ID.name: Indonesia
facts: Indonesia is the largest archipelago in the world with over 17,000 islands.
Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards, are found only in Indonesia.
Indonesia has the third-largest tropical rainforest in the world after Brazil and Congo.
Bali, one of Indonesia's islands, is one of the world's top tourist destinations.
Indonesia is the world's largest island country and the 4th most populous nation.

IE.name: Ireland
facts: Ireland has no snakes — legend credits Saint Patrick with driving them out.
Halloween originated in Ireland from the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain.
Ireland is home to over 30,000 castles and ruins.
The harp, not the shamrock, is Ireland's official national symbol.
Ireland's population is still lower than it was before the Great Famine of the 1840s.

IL.name: Israel
facts: Israel has more museums per capita than any other country.
Hebrew was a dead language for 1,700 years before being revived in Israel.
The Dead Sea, bordering Israel and Jordan, is the lowest point on Earth's surface.
Israel leads the world in recycled water use — over 85% of wastewater is recycled.
Israel has more startups per capita than any other country.

IN.name: India
facts: India has the most post offices of any country in the world — over 155,000.
The number zero was invented in India by mathematician Aryabhata.
India is the world's largest producer of spices and milk.
The Kumbh Mela gathering in India is visible from space due to the sheer number of people.
India's space program has sent missions to the Moon and Mars at costs lower than many Hollywood films.

IQ.name: Iraq
facts: Iraq is home to Mesopotamia, often called the 'Cradle of Civilization.'
The ancient city of Babylon, with its famous hanging gardens, was located in modern Iraq.
Writing was invented in Mesopotamia (Iraq) around 3400 BCE using cuneiform.
Iraq has the fifth-largest proven oil reserves in the world.
The Tigris and Euphrates rivers, which run through Iraq, supported the earliest known civilizations.

IR.name: Iran
facts: Iran is home to one of the world's oldest civilizations, dating back to 3200 BCE.
The Persian Empire was the largest empire in ancient history, spanning three continents.
Iran has 27 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
The concept of the postal system was invented in ancient Persia (modern-day Iran).
Tehran's Grand Bazaar is one of the oldest and largest bazaars in the Middle East.

IS.name: Iceland
facts: Iceland has no army, navy, or air force.
About 60% of Iceland's population lives in the capital area of Reykjavik.
Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was established in 930 AD — one of the oldest in the world.
Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, with parts on both the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.
There are no mosquitoes in Iceland.

IT.name: Italy
facts: Italy has the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites of any country in the world.
The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is the oldest university in continuous operation.
Italy is home to two independent countries within its borders: Vatican City and San Marino.
Italians invented the piano, espresso machine, and eyeglasses.
The Colosseum in Rome could hold 50,000–80,000 spectators.

JM.name: Jamaica
facts: Jamaica is the birthplace of reggae music and the legendary Bob Marley.
Usain Bolt, the fastest person ever timed, is Jamaican.
Jamaica was the first Caribbean country to gain independence, in 1962.
Blue Mountain coffee from Jamaica is considered one of the finest in the world.
Jamaica's flag is the only national flag that doesn't contain red, white, or blue.

JO.name: Jordan
facts: Petra, Jordan's famous ancient city carved into rock, is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Jordan borders the Dead Sea, the lowest point on Earth at 430 meters below sea level.
Wadi Rum desert in Jordan was used as a filming location for 'The Martian' and 'Lawrence of Arabia.'
Jordan is one of the most water-scarce countries in the world.
Amman was originally built on seven hills, like Rome.

JP.name: Japan
facts: Japan is made up of 6,852 islands.
Japan has more than 1,500 earthquakes per year.
Vending machines in Japan sell everything from hot meals to umbrellas — there are over 5 million.
Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains have an average delay of only 17 seconds.
The Japanese concept of 'forest bathing' (shinrin-yoku) is a recognized form of stress therapy.

KE.name: Kenya
facts: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, the second-highest peak in Africa.
The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya, visible from space.
Kenya dominates long-distance running — Kenyan athletes have won countless Olympic and marathon medals.
M-Pesa, the world's leading mobile money service, was invented in Kenya.
The annual wildebeest migration in Kenya's Masai Mara is one of the greatest wildlife spectacles on Earth.

KG.name: Kyrgyzstan
facts: Kyrgyzstan is over 90% mountainous, with peaks reaching above 7,000 meters.
Lake Issyk-Kul is one of the largest alpine lakes in the world and never freezes despite the altitude.
The Epic of Manas, Kyrgyzstan's national epic poem, is 20 times longer than the Iliad and Odyssey combined.
Traditional yurt culture is still practiced by nomadic communities.
Kyrgyzstan was the first Central Asian country to adopt a parliamentary system.

KH.name: Cambodia
facts: Cambodia's Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world.
The Cambodian flag is the only national flag to feature a building (Angkor Wat).
The Tonlé Sap lake doubles in size during the monsoon season.
Cambodia's Khmer Empire once controlled much of Southeast Asia.
Cambodia uses the US dollar alongside its own currency in everyday transactions.

KM.name: Comoros
facts: Comoros is one of the world's largest producers of ylang-ylang, used in perfumes.
The country consists of three main volcanic islands in the Indian Ocean off East Africa.
Mount Karthala on Grande Comore is one of the world's most active volcanoes.
Comoros has had over 20 coups or attempted coups since independence in 1975.
The coelacanth, a 'living fossil' fish thought extinct for millions of years, was found near Comoros.

KN.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
facts: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign state in the Americas by both area and population.
The country's citizenship-by-investment program, established in 1984, is the oldest of its kind.
Brimstone Hill Fortress is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the best-preserved forts in the Americas.
The islands were among the first Caribbean islands colonized by Europeans.
Mount Liamuiga, a dormant volcano on Saint Kitts, has a crater lake at its summit.

KP.name: North Korea
facts: North Korea uses its own calendar, called the Juche calendar, starting from 1912.
North Korea and South Korea are technically still at war — only an armistice was signed, not a peace treaty.
Pyongyang has a 105-story pyramid-shaped hotel (Ryugyong Hotel) that has never opened.
North Korea has its own intranet called Kwangmyong, separate from the global internet.
The DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) between North and South Korea has become an accidental wildlife refuge.

KR.name: South Korea
facts: South Korea has the fastest average internet speed in the world.
K-pop and Korean dramas (K-dramas) have become a global cultural phenomenon.
South Korea's Samsung produces about 20% of the country's GDP.
The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was specifically designed to be easy to learn.
South Korea has a 'Black Day' (April 14) where single people eat black bean noodles to commiserate.

KW.name: Kuwait
facts: The Kuwaiti Dinar is the highest-valued currency unit in the world.
Kuwait has no rivers or permanent bodies of fresh water.
Kuwait was one of the first Gulf states to establish a parliament.
The country gets almost all its fresh water from desalination plants.
Kuwait has some of the hottest temperatures ever recorded — up to 54°C.

KZ.name: Kazakhstan
facts: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.
The Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan was the launch site for the first human space flight.
Apples are believed to have originated in Kazakhstan — the name 'Almaty' means 'Father of Apples.'
Kazakhstan spans two continents: Europe and Asia.
The country is the 9th largest in the world by area.

LA.name: Laos
facts: Laos is the most heavily bombed country per capita in history, due to the Vietnam War era.
The Plain of Jars contains thousands of mysterious stone jars, some over 2,000 years old.
Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.
The Mekong River runs along much of Laos's border and is the country's lifeline.
Luang Prabang, the former royal capital, is a UNESCO World Heritage city.

LB.name: Lebanon
facts: Lebanon's cedar tree is on its flag and has been famous since ancient times.
Beirut has been destroyed and rebuilt 7 times throughout history.
Byblos in Lebanon is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
The Phoenicians, who invented the alphabet, came from modern-day Lebanon.
Lebanon is smaller than Connecticut but has 18 recognized religious sects.

LC.name: Saint Lucia
facts: Saint Lucia's twin Pitons — volcanic spires rising from the sea — are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Saint Lucia is the only country in the world named after a woman (Saint Lucy).
The island has two Nobel laureates — the highest per capita of any country.
Saint Lucia changed hands between Britain and France 14 times before becoming permanently British.
The Sulphur Springs near Soufrière is the world's only drive-in volcano.

LI.name: Liechtenstein
facts: Liechtenstein is the sixth-smallest country in the world.
It is one of only two doubly landlocked countries (surrounded entirely by landlocked countries).
Liechtenstein has no airport and no military.
The country is a major center for finance and has more registered companies than citizens.
Liechtenstein is the world's largest producer of false teeth.

LK.name: Sri Lanka
facts: Sri Lanka was known as Ceylon until 1972.
Sri Lanka is one of the world's largest tea exporters — Ceylon tea is famous worldwide.
The ancient city of Sigiriya features a palace built on top of a 200-meter rock fortress.
Sri Lanka has the highest biodiversity density in Asia.
Adam's Peak is a sacred mountain with a footprint-shaped mark revered by Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims, and Christians.

LR.name: Liberia
facts: Liberia was founded by freed American slaves in 1847 — its flag closely resembles the US flag.
Monrovia is named after US President James Monroe.
Liberia has the largest merchant shipping registry in the world.
Ellen Johnson Sirleaf of Liberia was the first elected female head of state in Africa.
Liberia is home to the last significant portion of Upper Guinea rainforest in West Africa.

LS.name: Lesotho
facts: Lesotho is the only country in the world entirely above 1,000 meters in elevation.
Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa — one of only three enclaved countries.
The country is known as the 'Kingdom in the Sky' due to its high altitude.
Lesotho's Thabana Ntlenyana is the highest peak in southern Africa at 3,482 meters.
The traditional Basotho blanket is a cultural icon and everyday garment.

LT.name: Lithuania
facts: Lithuanian is one of the oldest living languages in the world, closely related to Sanskrit.
Lithuania was the last pagan country in Europe, not Christianized until the 14th century.
The Hill of Crosses near Šiauliai has over 100,000 crosses placed by pilgrims.
Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence in 1990.
Vilnius's Old Town is one of the largest surviving medieval old towns in Northern Europe.

LU.name: Luxembourg
facts: Luxembourg has the highest GDP per capita in the world.
About 47% of Luxembourg's workforce commutes from neighboring countries.
Luxembourg was a founding member of the EU, NATO, and the United Nations.
The country has three official languages: Luxembourgish, French, and German.
Luxembourg City's old quarters and fortifications are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

LV.name: Latvia
facts: Latvia's flag is one of the oldest in the world, first mentioned in 1280.
Riga's Art Nouveau architecture district has one of the finest collections in Europe.
Latvia has the fourth-highest forest coverage in Europe at over 50%.
The first Christmas tree is said to have been erected in Riga in 1510.
Latvia is one of the Baltic states, along with Estonia and Lithuania.

LY.name: Libya
facts: Libya has the largest proven oil reserves in Africa.
The ancient Roman city of Leptis Magna in Libya is one of the best-preserved Roman ruins in the world.
About 90% of Libya is desert.
Libya's Saharan rock art in the Tadrart Acacus mountains dates back 12,000 years.
The Great Man-Made River in Libya is the world's largest irrigation project, drawing water from ancient underground aquifers.

MA.name: Morocco
facts: Morocco is home to the world's oldest university — the University of al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859 AD.
The Sahara Desert covers a large portion of southern Morocco.
Morocco is only 14 km from Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar.
Fez, Morocco has the world's oldest tannery still in operation.
Morocco was the first country to recognize the United States as an independent nation in 1777.

MC.name: Monaco
facts: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world, smaller than Central Park in New York.
Monaco has the highest population density of any country in the world.
The Monaco Grand Prix is one of the most prestigious Formula 1 races, held on city streets.
Monaco has no income tax, making it a haven for the ultra-wealthy.
The Monte Carlo Casino opened in 1863 and is one of the most famous casinos in the world.

MD.name: Moldova
facts: Moldova has the largest wine cellar in the world — Mileștii Mici has over 200 km of underground tunnels.
Moldova is one of the least visited countries in Europe.
The country is landlocked between Romania and Ukraine.
Wine production dates back over 5,000 years in Moldova.
Transnistria, a breakaway region, has its own government, currency, and military.

ME.name: Montenegro
facts: Montenegro's name means 'Black Mountain' in Venetian/Italian.
The Bay of Kotor is often called 'Europe's southernmost fjord.'
Montenegro gained independence from Serbia in 2006, making it one of Europe's newest countries.
Tara River Canyon is the deepest river canyon in Europe and second deepest in the world after the Grand Canyon.
Montenegro has one of the oldest olive trees in the world, believed to be over 2,000 years old.

MG.name: Madagascar
facts: About 90% of Madagascar's wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth.
Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world.
Lemurs are found only in Madagascar — there are over 100 species.
The Avenue of the Baobabs features 800-year-old trees lining a dirt road.
Madagascar separated from the Indian subcontinent about 88 million years ago.

MH.name: Marshall Islands
facts: The Marshall Islands were used as a US nuclear testing site — 67 bombs were detonated at Bikini Atoll.
The country consists of 29 coral atolls and 5 isolated islands.
Marshallese stick charts were an ancient navigation tool using shells and sticks to map ocean swells.
The Marshall Islands has one of the largest shark sanctuaries in the world.
The country's highest point is only about 10 meters above sea level.

MK.name: North Macedonia
facts: North Macedonia changed its name from 'Macedonia' in 2019 to resolve a decades-long dispute with Greece.
Mother Teresa was born in Skopje in 1910.
Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe, over 3 million years old.
Skopje was nearly destroyed by an earthquake in 1963 and rebuilt with international help.
North Macedonia's flag features a radiant golden sun on a red background.

ML.name: Mali
facts: Timbuktu in Mali was once a legendary center of learning and trade in the Islamic world.
The Great Mosque of Djenné is the largest mud-brick building in the world.
The Mali Empire (1235-1600) was one of the wealthiest empires in history.
Mansa Musa of Mali is considered the wealthiest person to have ever lived.
Malian music, especially the kora (harp), has influenced musicians worldwide.

MM.name: Myanmar
facts: Myanmar (formerly Burma) has over 10,000 Buddhist temples in the ancient city of Bagan.
Naypyidaw, the capital built in 2005, has 20-lane highways that are mostly empty.
Myanmar is one of only three countries that don't use the metric system (with the US and Liberia).
Inle Lake's leg-rowing fishermen are one of the country's most iconic sights.
Myanmar is the world's largest producer of rubies and jade.

MN.name: Mongolia
facts: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated country in the world.
Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire — the largest contiguous land empire in history.
About 30% of Mongolians are still nomadic or semi-nomadic herders.
Mongolia has more horses than people.
The Gobi Desert in southern Mongolia is the largest desert in Asia.

MR.name: Mauritania
facts: Mauritania's Eye of the Sahara (Richat Structure) is a 50-km-wide geological formation visible from space.
Nouakchott was a tiny village of 200 people before becoming the capital in 1960.
Mauritania was the last country to abolish slavery, doing so officially in 1981.
The ancient city of Chinguetti is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and was a center of Islamic learning.
Most of Mauritania is covered by the Sahara Desert.

MT.name: Malta
facts: Malta's megalithic temples are older than the pyramids of Egypt and Stonehenge.
Valletta is the smallest national capital in the EU by area.
Malta was awarded the George Cross by King George VI in 1942 for bravery in World War II.
The Maltese language is the only Semitic language written in Latin script.
Malta's Blue Lagoon on Comino island has crystal-clear turquoise waters.

MU.name: Mauritius
facts: The dodo bird was native to Mauritius and went extinct in the 17th century.
Mauritius has an underwater waterfall illusion visible from the air, caused by sand and silt patterns.
The country is one of Africa's wealthiest and most stable nations.
Mauritius's seven-colored earth in Chamarel is a natural phenomenon of multi-hued sand dunes.
Mark Twain reportedly said, 'Mauritius was made first, and then heaven.'

MV.name: Maldives
facts: The Maldives is the lowest-lying country in the world, with an average elevation of just 1.5 meters.
The Maldives consists of 1,192 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls.
Rising sea levels threaten the Maldives — it could be underwater by 2100.
The Maldives has some of the clearest water in the world with visibility up to 50 meters.
Malé is one of the most densely populated cities in the world.

MW.name: Malawi
facts: Lake Malawi contains more fish species than any other lake in the world — over 1,000.
Malawi is known as 'The Warm Heart of Africa' for its friendly people.
Lake Malawi makes up about a third of the country's total area.
Malawi is one of the most densely populated countries in Africa.
The country is one of the least developed in the world but has a rich cultural heritage.

MX.name: Mexico
facts: Mexico City was built on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán.
Mexico introduced chocolate, chili peppers, and corn to the world.
Mexico has 35 UNESCO World Heritage Sites — more than any other country in the Americas.
The Chichén Itzá pyramid creates a shadow of a serpent during the spring equinox.
Mexico City is sinking at a rate of about 50 cm per year due to water extraction from underground.

MY.name: Malaysia
facts: Malaysia's Petronas Twin Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.
Malaysia has one of the oldest tropical rainforests in the world — over 130 million years old.
The country is split into two parts separated by the South China Sea.
Malaysia is one of the world's top producers of palm oil and rubber.
The Rafflesia, the world's largest flower, can be found in Malaysian Borneo.

MZ.name: Mozambique
facts: Mozambique's flag features an AK-47 rifle — the only national flag with a modern firearm.
The country has over 2,500 km of Indian Ocean coastline.
Mozambique's Bazaruto Archipelago has some of the best marine life in the Indian Ocean.
The Island of Mozambique was a major Portuguese trading post and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Mozambique is home to Africa's second-largest lake — Lake Malawi/Niassa.

NA.name: Namibia
facts: Namibia's Namib Desert is considered the oldest desert in the world at about 55 million years.
Namibia was the first country in Africa to incorporate environmental protection into its constitution.
The Skeleton Coast is littered with shipwrecks and whale bones.
Namibia has one of the lowest population densities in the world.
The Sossusvlei sand dunes are among the tallest in the world, reaching over 300 meters.

NE.name: Niger
facts: Niger has the youngest population in the world with a median age of about 15 years.
The Sahara Desert covers about 80% of Niger's land area.
The Cure Salée festival celebrates the end of the rainy season with a massive gathering of nomadic peoples.
Niger is named after the Niger River, which flows through the southwestern part of the country.
The Air Mountains in Niger contain ancient rock carvings dating back thousands of years.

NG.name: Nigeria
facts: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa and the 6th most populous in the world.
Nollywood (Nigeria's film industry) produces more movies annually than Hollywood.
Nigeria has over 500 different ethnic groups and over 520 languages.
Lagos is the largest city in Africa with an estimated population of over 20 million.
Nigeria is Africa's largest economy and its biggest oil exporter.

NI.name: Nicaragua
facts: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America.
Lake Nicaragua is the only freshwater lake in the world with sharks (bull sharks).
Nicaragua has the second-largest rainforest in the Americas after the Amazon.
The country is known as the 'Land of Lakes and Volcanoes.'
Nicaragua's flag is one of only two national flags that contain purple (the other is Dominica).

NL.name: Netherlands
facts: About one-third of the Netherlands is below sea level.
The Netherlands has more bicycles than people — about 23 million bikes for 17.8 million people.
Amsterdam has over 1,200 bridges and 165 canals.
The Dutch are the tallest people in the world on average.
The Netherlands invented the stock exchange (Amsterdam Stock Exchange, 1602).

NO.name: Norway
facts: Norway has the world's longest road tunnel — the Lærdalstunnelen at 24.5 km.
Norway's Government Pension Fund is the largest sovereign wealth fund in the world.
The Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis) are visible in northern Norway.
Norway introduced salmon sushi to Japan in the 1980s.
Norway knighted a penguin — Brigadier Sir Nils Olav III at Edinburgh Zoo.

NP.name: Nepal
facts: Nepal is the only country in the world with a non-rectangular flag.
Mount Everest, the tallest mountain on Earth at 8,849m, is in Nepal.
Nepal has never been colonized by a foreign power.
Lumbini, Nepal is the birthplace of the Buddha.
Nepal's flag is made of two stacked triangles representing the Himalayas and two religions: Hinduism and Buddhism.

NR.name: Nauru
facts: Nauru is the smallest island country in the world at just 21 square kilometers.
Nauru was once the wealthiest country per capita due to phosphate mining.
The country has no official capital — Yaren is the de facto seat of government.
Nauru is the only country in the world with no official capital city.
Phosphate mining has left 80% of the island stripped and barren.

NZ.name: New Zealand
facts: New Zealand was the first country to give all women the right to vote in 1893.
There are more sheep than people in New Zealand — about 6 sheep per person.
New Zealand has no native land mammals (except bats) — it was dominated by birds before human arrival.
The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit trilogies were filmed entirely in New Zealand.
New Zealand is one of the last major landmasses settled by humans — around 1250-1300 AD.

OM.name: Oman
facts: Oman's frankincense trade dates back thousands of years and the trees grow in the Dhofar region.
The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque has the second-largest hand-woven carpet in the world.
Oman is one of the oldest inhabited regions in the Arabian Peninsula.
The country has dramatic landscapes from desert dunes to green mountain wadis.
Oman was one of the first Arab countries to allow women to vote.

PA.name: Panama
facts: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and handles about 5% of global trade.
Panama is the only place in the world where you can see the sun rise on the Pacific and set on the Atlantic.
Panama City has the only rainforest within a capital city's limits — Metropolitan Natural Park.
The Panama hat actually originated in Ecuador.
Panama was the first Latin American country to adopt the US dollar as legal tender.

PE.name: Peru
facts: Machu Picchu, the ancient Inca city, is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Peru has 90 different microclimates, making it one of the most diverse countries on Earth.
The potato originated in Peru — there are over 3,000 varieties grown there.
Lake Titicaca, shared with Bolivia, is the highest navigable lake in the world.
The Nazca Lines in Peru are ancient geoglyphs visible only from the air.

PG.name: Papua New Guinea
facts: Papua New Guinea has over 850 languages — more than any other country in the world.
The island of New Guinea is the second-largest island in the world after Greenland.
Many tribes in PNG's highlands had no contact with the outside world until the 20th century.
Birds of paradise, found in PNG, are among the most spectacular birds on Earth.
PNG has one of the largest areas of intact tropical rainforest outside the Amazon and Congo.

PH.name: Philippines
facts: The Philippines is made up of 7,641 islands.
The Philippines is the texting capital of the world — Filipinos send billions of texts monthly.
Jeepneys, colorfully decorated former military jeeps, are the most popular form of public transportation.
The Chocolate Hills of Bohol are over 1,200 cone-shaped hills that turn brown in dry season.
The Philippines has the longest Christmas celebration in the world — starting in September.

PK.name: Pakistan
facts: Pakistan has the world's second-highest mountain — K2 at 8,611 meters.
The ancient Indus Valley civilization, one of the world's oldest, was in modern Pakistan.
Pakistan's Karakoram Highway is one of the highest paved international roads in the world.
Pakistan is the world's fourth-largest producer of cotton.
The national sport of Pakistan is field hockey, in which they have won multiple Olympic medals.

PL.name: Poland
facts: Marie Curie, the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, was born in Poland.
Poland's Białowieża Forest is one of the last and largest primeval forests in Europe.
The Polish constitution of 1791 was the first modern constitution in Europe.
Kraków's St. Mary's Basilica plays a trumpet call every hour that stops mid-note — commemorating a 13th-century watchman shot by invaders.
Poland is the world's largest exporter of amber.

PS.name: Palestine
facts: Palestine is a UN observer state, recognized by over 140 countries.
The Old City of Jerusalem and Bethlehem's Church of the Nativity are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Palestine.
Jericho in the West Bank is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
Palestinian embroidery (tatreez) is a centuries-old art form recognized by UNESCO.
The Dead Sea, bordering Palestine, is the lowest point on Earth.

PT.name: Portugal
facts: Portugal is the oldest nation-state in Europe, with borders largely unchanged since 1249.
The Portuguese Empire was the first global empire and the longest-lasting European colonial empire.
Portugal decriminalized all drugs in 2001 and saw drug abuse rates drop significantly.
Lisbon is older than Rome — it's one of the oldest cities in Western Europe.
Portugal's Vasco da Gama Bridge is the longest bridge in Europe at 12.3 km.

PW.name: Palau
facts: Palau has some of the most pristine marine environments in the world.
Jellyfish Lake in Palau contains millions of golden jellyfish that have lost their sting.
Palau created one of the world's first shark sanctuaries in 2009.
The Rock Islands Southern Lagoon is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Palau's passport contains a pledge to protect the environment that visitors must sign.

PY.name: Paraguay
facts: Paraguay is one of only two landlocked countries in South America (with Bolivia).
Paraguay's flag has different emblems on each side — the only national flag with this feature.
The Itaipu Dam on the Paraguay-Brazil border is one of the largest hydroelectric plants in the world.
Guarani is co-official with Spanish, making Paraguay one of the few bilingual nations by law.
The Chaco region covers 60% of Paraguay but has less than 2% of the population.

QA.name: Qatar
facts: Qatar has the highest GDP per capita in the world, driven by natural gas and oil.
Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup — the first Middle Eastern country to do so.
Al Jazeera, one of the world's largest news networks, is headquartered in Qatar.
Qatar's flag is the only national flag with a width more than twice its height.
The Pearl-Qatar is an artificial island with luxury residences and shopping.

RO.name: Romania
facts: Bram Stoker's Dracula was inspired by Vlad the Impaler, a Romanian prince.
Romania's Palace of the Parliament is the heaviest building in the world.
The Danube Delta in Romania is Europe's largest wetland and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
Romania is home to Europe's largest population of brown bears.
Romanian is the closest living language to Latin.

RS.name: Serbia
facts: Belgrade is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Europe.
Nikola Tesla, the famous inventor, was an ethnic Serb born in modern-day Croatia.
Serbia is one of the largest exporters of raspberries in the world.
The Danube River flows through Serbia, including the dramatic Iron Gates gorge.
Serbia's Đavolja Varoš (Devil's Town) features eerie rock formations created by erosion.

RU.name: Russia
facts: Russia is the largest country in the world, spanning 11 time zones.
Lake Baikal in Russia holds 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater.
The Moscow Metro is famous for its palatial stations with chandeliers, mosaics, and marble.
Russia sent the first human (Yuri Gagarin) and the first satellite (Sputnik) into space.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world at 9,289 km.

RW.name: Rwanda
facts: Rwanda is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Hills' for its stunning hilly landscape.
Kigali is considered one of the cleanest cities in Africa.
Rwanda has the highest percentage of women in parliament of any country in the world.
Mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park are one of Rwanda's biggest attractions.
Rwanda banned single-use plastic bags in 2008, one of the first countries to do so.

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
facts: Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers — it's the largest country in the world without one.
Saudi Arabia is home to Mecca and Medina, the two holiest cities in Islam.
The country has the world's largest sand desert — the Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter).
Saudi Arabia allowed women to drive starting in 2018.
The country holds about 16% of the world's proven petroleum reserves.

SB.name: Solomon Islands
facts: The Solomon Islands were a major battleground in World War II, especially during the Battle of Guadalcanal.
The country has over 900 islands and some of the most biodiverse marine environments on Earth.
Many islanders still use shell money for traditional ceremonies.
Kennedy Island is named after JFK, whose PT-109 boat was sunk nearby in WWII.
The Solomon Islands have some of the last uncontacted tribes in the Pacific.

SC.name: Seychelles
facts: The Seychelles is the smallest country in Africa by population.
The coco de mer palm produces the world's largest seed, weighing up to 25 kg.
Aldabra Atoll is a UNESCO World Heritage Site home to over 100,000 giant tortoises.
The Seychelles has the highest human development index in Africa.
The islands' granite formations make them some of the oldest oceanic islands on Earth.

SD.name: Sudan
facts: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt — over 200 ancient Nubian pyramids at Meroë.
The Blue and White Nile rivers merge at Khartoum.
Sudan was the largest country in Africa before South Sudan's independence in 2011.
The ancient Kingdom of Kush in northern Sudan rivaled Egypt in power and wealth.
Suakin on the Red Sea coast has ruins of a once-thriving coral-block city.

SE.name: Sweden
facts: Sweden hasn't been at war since 1814 — the longest period of peace for any European nation.
IKEA, Spotify, and Minecraft were all created in Sweden.
Sweden recycles so well it has to import garbage from other countries to fuel its waste-to-energy plants.
The Nobel Prizes (except Peace) are awarded in Stockholm.
Sweden has the right of public access ('Allemansrätten') allowing anyone to roam freely in nature.

SG.name: Singapore
facts: Singapore is both a city and a country — one of only three city-states in the world.
Chewing gum has been banned in Singapore since 1992.
Singapore's Changi Airport has been voted the world's best airport for years running.
Despite its small size, Singapore is one of the world's busiest ports.
Singapore has four official languages: English, Malay, Mandarin, and Tamil.

SI.name: Slovenia
facts: Slovenia has the third-highest forest coverage in Europe at nearly 60%.
Lake Bled, with its island church and cliffside castle, is one of Europe's most photographed places.
Slovenia became the first former communist country to host the G20 summit.
Postojna Cave has a unique cave-dwelling creature called the 'human fish' (olm).
Melania Trump, former US First Lady, was born in Slovenia.

SK.name: Slovakia
facts: Slovakia has more castles and châteaux per capita than any other country — over 180.
Bratislava is the only capital in the world that borders two other countries (Austria and Hungary).
The Demänovská Cave of Liberty is one of the longest caves in Europe.
Slovakia and Czechia peacefully split into two countries in 1993 — the 'Velvet Divorce.'
Andy Warhol's parents were from Slovakia.

SL.name: Sierra Leone
facts: Sierra Leone means 'Lion Mountains,' named by Portuguese explorers.
Freetown was founded in 1792 as a home for freed slaves from Britain and the Americas.
The country is one of the world's major producers of diamonds.
Sierra Leone has some of the most beautiful beaches in West Africa.
The cotton tree in Freetown, over 500 years old, is a national symbol.

SM.name: San Marino
facts: San Marino claims to be the oldest republic in the world, founded in 301 AD.
San Marino is entirely surrounded by Italy and is one of the smallest countries in Europe.
The country has more vehicles than people.
San Marino's Three Towers on Monte Titano are the national symbol and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
San Marino has one of the lowest unemployment rates in Europe.

SN.name: Senegal
facts: Senegal is known as the 'Gateway to Africa' due to its westernmost location on the continent.
Dakar was the finishing point of the famous Paris-Dakar Rally for decades.
Senegal's Lac Rose (Pink Lake) has waters that turn bright pink due to algae.
Teranga, meaning 'hospitality,' is a core cultural value in Senegal.
Senegal has never had a military coup, making it one of Africa's most stable democracies.

SO.name: Somalia
facts: Somalia has the longest coastline in mainland Africa at over 3,000 km.
Camel milk is a staple food — Somalia has more camels than any other country.
The ancient port city of Mogadishu was once a major Indian Ocean trading hub.
Somali is one of the few African languages with its own written script (since 1972).
Laas Geel in Somalia has some of the earliest known rock art in Africa, dating back 5,000 years.

SR.name: Suriname
facts: Suriname is the smallest country in South America.
Dutch is the official language — the only country in South America where Dutch is spoken.
Over 90% of Suriname is covered by tropical rainforest.
Paramaribo's historic inner city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Suriname is one of the most ethnically diverse countries in the world.

SS.name: South Sudan
facts: South Sudan is the world's newest country, gaining independence from Sudan in 2011.
The Sudd is one of the largest wetlands in the world, fed by the White Nile.
South Sudan has the largest annual land mammal migration — over a million white-eared kob.
Oil accounts for nearly all of South Sudan's export revenue.
The country has over 60 different ethnic groups and languages.

ST.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
facts: São Tomé and Príncipe is the smallest Portuguese-speaking country in the world.
The islands sit on the equator in the Gulf of Guinea.
São Tomé was once the world's largest producer of sugar in the 16th century.
Pico Cão Grande is a dramatic volcanic plug that rises 370 meters from the jungle floor.
The islands were uninhabited until Portuguese arrival in the 15th century.

SV.name: El Salvador
facts: El Salvador is the smallest and most densely populated country in Central America.
El Salvador became the first country to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender in 2021.
The country has over 20 volcanoes, including the active Izalco volcano once called 'Lighthouse of the Pacific.'
El Salvador's name means 'The Savior' in Spanish.
Pupusas, thick corn tortillas filled with cheese and beans, are the national dish.

SY.name: Syria
facts: Damascus is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
Syria is home to some of the earliest evidence of agriculture, dating back 10,000 years.
The ancient city of Palmyra was a major trading center on the Silk Road.
Aleppo's souq (market) was one of the largest covered markets in the world.
Syria has six UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Ancient City of Damascus.

SZ.name: Eswatini
facts: Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) is one of the last absolute monarchies in the world.
The annual Reed Dance ceremony involves tens of thousands of young women.
Eswatini is one of the smallest countries in Africa.
The country changed its name from Swaziland to Eswatini in 2018.
Eswatini is almost entirely surrounded by South Africa, with a small border with Mozambique.

TD.name: Chad
facts: Lake Chad was once one of the largest lakes in Africa but has shrunk by 90% since the 1960s.
Chad is named after Lake Chad, which means 'large expanse of water' in a local language.
The Ennedi Plateau in Chad has dramatic sandstone arches and ancient rock art.
Chad's flag is almost identical to Romania's flag, differing only in a slightly darker shade of blue.
The Sahara Desert covers the northern third of Chad.

TG.name: Togo
facts: Togo is one of the smallest countries in Africa, shaped like a narrow strip.
The Tamberma Valley's fortified mud houses (Batammariba) are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Togo was a German colony before becoming French after World War I.
Lomé's Grand Marché is one of the largest markets in West Africa, run primarily by women.
Togo is one of the world's largest producers of phosphate.

TH.name: Thailand
facts: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country never colonized by a European power.
Bangkok's full ceremonial name is 168 characters long — the longest city name in the world.
Thailand was known as Siam until 1939.
Muay Thai (Thai boxing) is the national sport and a major cultural tradition.
Thailand is the world's largest exporter of rice.

TJ.name: Tajikistan
facts: Over 90% of Tajikistan is mountainous, including peaks above 7,000 meters.
The Pamir Highway is one of the highest and most remote roads in the world.
Ismoil Somoni Peak at 7,495 meters is the highest point in Central Asia.
Tajikistan produces nearly all of its electricity from hydropower.
The Fann Mountains have turquoise lakes considered among the most beautiful in Central Asia.

TL.name: Timor-Leste
facts: Timor-Leste (East Timor) is one of the youngest countries in the world, gaining independence in 2002.
The country occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor in Southeast Asia.
Ataúro Island off the coast has some of the highest marine biodiversity in the world.
Coffee is the main export, with the Arabica variety grown in highland areas.
Timor-Leste was under Portuguese rule for over 400 years before Indonesian occupation in 1975.

TM.name: Turkmenistan
facts: The Darvaza Gas Crater, called the 'Door to Hell,' has been burning since 1971.
Ashgabat holds the Guinness Record for the most marble-clad buildings in the world.
Turkmenistan has the fourth-largest natural gas reserves in the world.
The country's Akhal-Teke horse breed is known as the 'golden horse' and is a national symbol.
Turkmenistan is one of the most closed and isolated countries in the world.

TN.name: Tunisia
facts: The ancient city of Carthage, near Tunis, was once the rival of Rome.
Star Wars scenes for Tatooine were filmed in southern Tunisia — the planet's name comes from the Tunisian town Tataouine.
Tunisia was the birthplace of the Arab Spring in 2010-2011.
The Bardo Museum in Tunis has the world's largest collection of Roman mosaics.
Tunisia has the oldest synagogue in Africa — the El Ghriba synagogue on Djerba island.

TO.name: Tonga
facts: Tonga is the only remaining monarchy in the Pacific Islands.
Tonga was never formally colonized by a European power.
The Tongan language has one of the smallest alphabets in the world with just 17 letters.
Humpback whales migrate to Tonga's waters each year to breed and give birth.
The 2022 Hunga Tonga volcanic eruption was one of the most powerful in modern history.

TR.name: Turkey
facts: Istanbul is the only city in the world that spans two continents — Europe and Asia.
Turkey introduced coffee to Europe — the word 'coffee' comes from the Turkish 'kahve.'
The ancient city of Troy, from Homer's Iliad, was located in modern Turkey.
Turkey has more ancient Greek ruins than Greece itself.
Santa Claus (Saint Nicholas) was born in Patara, in modern-day Turkey.

TT.name: Trinidad and Tobago
facts: Trinidad and Tobago is the birthplace of steel pan drums and calypso music.
Pitch Lake in Trinidad is the world's largest natural deposit of asphalt.
Trinidad Carnival is one of the biggest and most famous carnivals in the world.
The country has the third-highest GDP per capita in the Americas after the US and Canada.
Tobago is believed to be the inspiration for Robinson Crusoe's island.

TV.name: Tuvalu
facts: Tuvalu is the fourth-smallest country in the world by land area.
The country earns millions from licensing its '.tv' internet domain.
Tuvalu's highest point is only 4.6 meters above sea level, making it extremely vulnerable to sea-level rise.
Tuvalu has no streams or rivers — freshwater comes from rainwater collection.
The total land area of Tuvalu is only about 26 square kilometers.

TZ.name: Tanzania
facts: Mount Kilimanjaro, the tallest mountain in Africa, is in Tanzania.
The Serengeti hosts the largest annual migration of animals on Earth.
Zanzibar, part of Tanzania, was once the world's leading clove producer.
Tanzania is home to the Olduvai Gorge, one of the most important paleoanthropological sites.
Tanzanite, a precious gemstone, is found only in Tanzania.

UA.name: Ukraine
facts: Ukraine is the largest country entirely within Europe.
Kyiv's metro system includes one of the deepest stations in the world — Arsenalna at 105.5 meters.
Ukraine's flag represents blue sky over golden wheat fields.
The Chernobyl exclusion zone has become an unintentional wildlife refuge.
Ukraine is one of the world's largest exporters of sunflower oil.

UG.name: Uganda
facts: Uganda is home to half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas.
Lake Victoria, which borders Uganda, is the largest lake in Africa.
The source of the Nile River is at Jinja, Uganda.
Winston Churchill called Uganda 'the Pearl of Africa.'
Uganda has one of the youngest populations in the world with a median age of about 15.

US.name: United States
facts: The US has no official language at the federal level.
Alaska is simultaneously the most northern, western, and eastern state (the Aleutian Islands cross the 180° meridian).
The US interstate highway system requires that one mile in every five must be straight — allegedly to serve as emergency airstrips.
The Library of Congress is the largest library in the world with over 170 million items.
Yellowstone National Park sits on top of a supervolcano.

UY.name: Uruguay
facts: Uruguay hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930.
Uruguay was the first country in the world to fully legalize cannabis.
Nearly 95% of Uruguay's electricity comes from renewable sources.
Uruguay has more cattle than people — about 3.5 cows per person.
Uruguay is one of the most progressive countries in Latin America for LGBTQ+ rights.

UZ.name: Uzbekistan
facts: Uzbekistan has some of the most stunning Silk Road architecture in the world, especially in Samarkand.
The Registan in Samarkand is considered one of the most beautiful public squares on Earth.
Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world (with Liechtenstein).
The Aral Sea, once the fourth-largest lake in the world, has mostly dried up due to Soviet-era irrigation.
Tashkent's metro stations are decorated like palaces with marble and chandeliers.

VA.name: Vatican City
facts: Vatican City is the smallest independent state in the world at just 0.44 square kilometers.
The Vatican has its own post office, radio station, and railway station.
St. Peter's Basilica is one of the largest churches in the world.
The Sistine Chapel ceiling, painted by Michelangelo, is one of the most famous artworks in history.
Vatican City has the highest crime rate per capita of any state — mostly petty theft by tourists.

VC.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
facts: The Grenadines islands were filming locations for Pirates of the Caribbean.
La Soufrière volcano erupted in April 2021, forcing mass evacuations.
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines consists of 32 islands, only 9 of which are inhabited.
The Tobago Cays Marine Park has some of the best snorkeling in the Caribbean.
The country gained independence from Britain in 1979.

VE.name: Venezuela
facts: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world at 979 meters.
Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world.
Lightning strikes over Lake Maracaibo up to 300 nights per year — a phenomenon called Catatumbo Lightning.
Venezuela is named after Venice ('Little Venice') by European explorers.
Venezuela has won more international beauty pageant titles than almost any other country.

VN.name: Vietnam
facts: Vietnam is the world's largest exporter of cashews and second-largest coffee exporter.
Halong Bay has nearly 2,000 limestone islands and islets.
Vietnam has the world's largest cave — Sơn Đoòng — large enough to fit a 40-story skyscraper.
Motorbikes outnumber cars 20:1 in Vietnam.
Vietnamese is a tonal language with six different tones.

VU.name: Vanuatu
facts: Vanuatu has the highest density of languages per capita in the world — over 100 languages for 320,000 people.
Land diving on Pentecost Island, where men jump from tall towers with vines tied to their ankles, inspired bungee jumping.
Mount Yasur on Tanna Island is one of the most accessible active volcanoes in the world.
Vanuatu is consistently ranked as one of the happiest countries by the Happy Planet Index.
Vanuatu has no income tax or wealth tax.

WS.name: Samoa
facts: Samoa was the first Polynesian country to gain independence, in 1962.
Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island, spent his last years in Samoa and is buried there.
In 2011, Samoa skipped an entire day (December 30) by switching to the west side of the International Date Line.
Traditional Samoan culture (fa'a Samoa) remains one of the strongest in the Pacific.
Samoan tattoo tradition (tatau) is the origin of the English word 'tattoo.'

XK.name: Kosovo
facts: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008 and is recognized by over 100 UN member states.
Kosovo has one of the youngest populations in Europe with a median age around 29.
The Visoki Dečani monastery is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Kosovo's Rugova Canyon is one of the longest canyons in Europe.
Pristina has a vibrant café culture with one of the highest cafés-per-capita in Europe.

YE.name: Yemen
facts: Yemen is home to the ancient city of Sana'a, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with distinctive multi-story mud buildings.
Socotra Island has landscapes so alien that it's been called the 'Galápagos of the Indian Ocean.'
Yemen was the first country in the Arabian Peninsula to grant women the right to vote.
Mocha, Yemen is the origin of the word 'mocha' — it was a major coffee-exporting port.
The Old Walled City of Shibam has been called 'the Manhattan of the desert' for its mud skyscrapers.

ZA.name: South Africa
facts: South Africa has 11 official languages — more than almost any country.
South Africa is the only country to have voluntarily dismantled its nuclear weapons.
The first successful heart transplant was performed in Cape Town by Dr. Christiaan Barnard in 1967.
Table Mountain in Cape Town is one of the oldest mountains in the world — over 600 million years old.
South Africa has the third-largest biodiversity in the world.

ZM.name: Zambia
facts: Victoria Falls, on Zambia's border with Zimbabwe, is one of the largest waterfalls in the world.
The local name for Victoria Falls is Mosi-oa-Tunya, meaning 'The Smoke That Thunders.'
Zambia has one of the largest copper deposits in the world, in the Copperbelt Province.
The country was named after the Zambezi River.
Zambia is home to the South Luangwa National Park, famous for walking safaris.

ZW.name: Zimbabwe
facts: Great Zimbabwe ruins gave the country its name — 'Zimbabwe' means 'houses of stone.'
Zimbabwe shares Victoria Falls with Zambia.
Zimbabwe experienced hyperinflation so extreme that it printed a 100-trillion-dollar note.
The country has the highest number of official languages in the world — 16.
Hwange National Park is one of Africa's largest game reserves, famous for its elephant herds.
